name: Continental W670-6A / R-670-5 seven-cylinder radial (Boeing-Stearman PT-17), 220 hp
summary: Seven-cylinder single-row air-cooled radial, direct drive, carburetted and confirmed unsupercharged. It fires every other cylinder (1-3-5-7-2-4-6) at even 102.9 deg intervals and turns only about 2,000 rpm, so the sound is a slow, loping bark through short stacks or a collector ring.

cylinders.note: Wilkinson 1945, p.87: '7 cylinders, 1-row radial, air cooled, direct drive, not supercharged, 4-cycle. A.T.C. 162.'

supercharger.note: Wilkinson 1945, p.87, W-670-M data page: 'Supercharger: None'; the W-670-6A (R-670-5) and W-670-K entries on the same page each say 'Direct drive. Not supercharged.' This is the confirmation required to include a radial. The same book says Kinner's five-cylinder K-5, B-5 and R-5 are also 'none of which are supercharged', if a five-cylinder alternative is wanted.

bore_mm.note: 5.125 in on the page (book rounds to 130 mm); converted by me. Same bore in the Radial Engines Ltd catalogue and the AEHS history.

stroke_mm.note: 4.625 in on the page (book rounds to 117 mm); converted by me.

displacement_cc.note: 668 cu in (book: 10.9 litres); converted by me. AEHS gives 667.9 cu in.

compression_ratio.note: W670-6A, -6N, -17, -11A (Radial Engines Ltd table of specifications); AEHS's table from Type Certificate 162 agrees. The W670-M is 6.1:1 (Wilkinson, AEHS).

firing_order.note: Radial Engines Ltd table of specifications; Wings of History museum page for the R-670-5 gives the same. Numbering convention is not stated on either page (the usual radial convention is No. 1 at top, numbered in the direction of rotation).

firing_intervals_deg.note: Not stated on the page: 720/7, my calculation from a single-throw crank and the firing order above. Even firing.

crank.value: single throw, two-piece counterbalanced crankshaft in two ball bearings; one master rod on cylinder No. 1 carrying six link rods
crank.note: Crankshaft from Wilkinson p.87. Master rod location '#1 cylinder' from the Radial Engines Ltd catalogue. Six link rods on knuckle pins is from the AEHS description of the A-70, the W670's direct predecessor.

valves_per_cylinder.note: '1 inlet valve and 1 exhaust valve (sodium cooled) per cylinder actuated by push rods.' AEHS describes the predecessor A-70's enclosed valve gear as a double cam ring, tubular push rods and rocker arms.

ivo_atdc.note: Catalogue wording: 'Intake opens @ 4 ATC', i.e. after top centre, not before. Measured with No. 1 cylinder valve clearance set to 0.124 in cold (a timing-check clearance; running clearance is 0.010 in cold), so real opening at running clearance is earlier. Source is an overhaul shop's mechanics handbook, not a Continental manual.

ivc_abdc.note: At 0.124 in checking clearance; see ivo note.

evo_bbdc.note: At 0.124 in checking clearance; see ivo note.

evc_atdc.note: 'Exhaust closes @ TDC', at 0.124 in checking clearance; see ivo note.

ignition_timing.value: right magneto 32 deg BTDC, left magneto 29 deg BTDC; two plugs per cylinder
ignition_timing.note: AEHS gives the same magneto timing; two plugs per cylinder from Wilkinson.

peak_power_kw.note: 220 hp; pilotfriend gives '220 hp (164 kw)'. Rating of 220 hp at 2,075 rpm (take-off and normal, sea level) is from Wilkinson for the W-670-6A (R-670-5), and matches the catalogue and Type Certificate 162 as quoted by AEHS. The Wings of History museum page says 225 hp at 2200 rpm for its R-670-5; Wikipedia's R-670-K entry is 225 hp at 2,175 rpm.

peak_power_rpm.note: Rated (take-off and normal) speed; aircraft engines of this type have no separate redline, so use this as the maximum.

redline_rpm.note: Rated maximum rpm for the -6A; 2,200 rpm for the 240 hp W670-M.

cruise_rating.note: This cruise figure is for the W-670-M (240 hp at 2,200 take-off); given for scale only.

intake_type.value: single updraft Bendix-Stromberg NA-R6 carburettor feeding induction passages in the rear crankcase section and one intake pipe per cylinder; no blower
intake_type.note: Carburettor from Wilkinson; venturi 1-15/16 in per AEHS (Type Certificate 162 table). Induction passages in the rear crankcase section are described by AEHS for the A-70 family.

throttle_dia_mm.note: Carburettor venturi diameter 1-15/16 in (not the throttle bore); converted by me.

exhaust_notes.value: One exhaust port per cylinder; variants differ in front- or rear-facing exhausts. A Type Test report mentions an exhaust collector ring and individual exhaust stacks.

engine_dry_weight_lb.note: W670-6A, from Type Certificate 162 table; the catalogue says approx. 485 lb.

missing: rod_length_mm (master rod and link rod lengths)
valve timing at running clearance, and from a Continental manual (the overhaul and operator manuals are sold by aircorpslibrary.com and were not readable)
peak_torque_nm and rpm (not published; torque at rating can be derived from 220 hp at 2,075 rpm)
exhaust stack length and diameter, collector ring dimensions
cylinder numbering convention and direction of rotation, from a page

sources.what: Paul H. Wilkinson, 'Aircraft Engines of the World 1945', scanned at the Internet Archive; W-670 data page (p.87) read from the OCR text. Standard reference; states 'Supercharger: None'.

Radial Engines, Ltd. (Guthrie, Oklahoma overhaul shop) 'Parts Catalog and Mechanics Handbook for Jacobs R755, Continental W670 & Lycoming R680', Summer 2020: table of specifications with firing order, master rod location and valve timing. Vendor document.
Aircraft Engine Historical Society, 'Continental's Radial Aircraft Engines': construction history and a specification table transcribed from Type Certificate No. 162.
Wings of History Air Museum page for its R-670-5: firing order and basic specifications.
pilotfriend engine summary: 220 hp (164 kW), bore and stroke.
Wikipedia, Continental R-670: variants and Jane's 1938 specifications (its supercharger line is blank, so it was not used as confirmation).
